text: For a function f: R^2 -> R, which implication is correct?
choices: If f is differentiable at a point, then both partial derivatives exist there
If both partial derivatives exist at a point, then f is differentiable there
If both partial derivatives exist at a point, then f is continuous there
If all directional derivatives exist at a point, then f is differentiable there
explanation: Differentiability implies existence of all partial derivatives (and continuity). The converses fail: partial derivatives can exist where f is discontinuous (e.g. xy/(x^2+y^2)), and even every directional derivative can exist at a point where f is not differentiable. Continuity of the partials is what guarantees differentiability.
